lessons.title: 昼と夜の営業時間を確かめる
lessons.objective: Explain this restaurant’s lunch, afternoon break, last order, and evening reopening to a fellow traveler, then verify the exact time with staff.
lessons.focus: 昼の営業 and 夜の営業 distinguish lunch and evening service. ラストオーダー is the last kitchen order. 休憩時間 marks the interval between services. 店員に確認しましょう turns an assumption into a checked fact.

reader.speaker: Femke

reader.en: Do some people drink coffee and talk after eating?

reader.speaker: Daniel

reader.en: Some do, but each restaurant has its own hours.

lessons.title: 混んだ屋台で友人に注文を任せる
lessons.objective: Coach a friend through ordering at a busy yakitori stall with short Japanese commands, then let the friend state quantities, choose seasoning, and pay.
lessons.focus: ～を注文して, ～を選んで, and ～を伝えて are short conversational commands. 焼き鳥 is grilled chicken skewers, 本 counts skewers, and たれ／塩 distinguish sauce and salt seasoning. 今度はあなたの番です hands the task to the friend.
lessons.scene: Daniel helps Aiko order at a crowded evening yakitori stall, then steps back so she completes the order.

reader.speaker: Daniel

reader.speaker: Daniel

reader.speaker: Aiko

reader.en: Two thigh skewers and one meatball skewer with sauce, please.

lessons.title: 暑い屋台の生魚を断る
lessons.objective: Tell a friend directly why you will not buy unrefrigerated raw fish from a hot afternoon cart, name food poisoning and upset stomach, and suggest a different meal without embarrassing the friend.
lessons.focus: 生魚 means raw fish, 冷蔵 means refrigeration, 氷 means ice, 食中毒 means food poisoning, and お腹をこわす means to get an upset stomach. 買わないで and 代わりに…にしよう express a quiet refusal and alternative.
lessons.scene: At four on a hot afternoon, Diego wants raw-fish rice from an unrefrigerated cart. Emma speaks to him quietly.

lessons.title: 新しい料理に具体的な感想を伝える
lessons.objective: Give the owner sincere, detailed feedback on a new vegetarian hot sandwich, praise its texture and presentation, make one tactful suggestion about salt, and say you would order it again.

cards.en: I hope you keep it on the menu. I would order it again.

cards.ja: 好意で率直にお伝えしています。
cards.en: I am telling you honestly and kindly.

reader.speaker: Daniel

lessons.title: 熱い鉄板による火傷を時系列で報告する
lessons.objective: Narrate when and how a guest burned his hand, report the blister and redness, ask the manager to record the incident, and request directions to medical help.
lessons.focus: 午後二時十五分 names the exact time; そのとき／そのあと／少しして order the events. 火傷, 水ぶくれ, and 赤み name the injury findings directly.
lessons.scene: Claire and Ben are at a small lunch restaurant when Ben grasps a smoking iron skillet handle.

cards.ja: 午後二時十五分に、熱い鉄板が運ばれてきました。
cards.en: At 2:15 p.m., the hot skillet was brought to us.

cards.ja: そのとき、ベンがナプキンを使わずに取っ手をつかみました。
cards.en: At that moment, Ben grabbed the handle without a napkin.

cards.ja: そのあと、手を水道水の下に当てました。
cards.en: After that, we held his hand under tap water.

cards.ja: 少しして、手のひらに水ぶくれができました。
cards.en: A little later, a blister formed on his palm.

cards.ja: 手全体に、まだ焼けるような痛みがあります。
cards.en: I still feel burning pain across my hand.

cards.ja: この火傷を事故記録に書いていただけますか。
cards.en: Could you record this burn in the incident log?

cards.ja: 報告書の写しをいただけますか。
cards.en: Could I have a copy of the report?

cards.ja: 一番近い診療所はどこですか。
目撃した店員の名前はジュリアンさんです。
cards.en: The employee who witnessed it is named Julián.

cards.ja: 正確な時刻と名前を記録してください。
cards.en: Please record the exact time and name.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: クレアとベンが昼食を食べていたとき、ベンが手を火傷しました。
reader.en: While Claire and Ben were eating lunch, Ben burned his hand.

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: 何が起きたか教えてください。報告書に正確な時刻が必要です。
reader.en: Please tell me what happened. I need the exact time for my report.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: 午後二時十五分に、熱い鉄板が運ばれてきました。
reader.en: At 2:15 p.m., the hot skillet was brought to us.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: 店員のジュリアンさんがテーブルに置き、鉄板からはまだ煙が出ていました。
reader.en: Julián, the server, set it on the table, and the skillet was still smoking.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: そのとき、ベンがナプキンを使わずに取っ手をつかみました。
reader.en: At that moment, Ben grabbed the handle without a napkin.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: そのあと、手を水道水の下に当てました。
reader.en: After that, we held his hand under tap water.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: 少しして、手のひらに水ぶくれができました。
reader.en: A little later, a blister formed on his palm.

reader.speaker: Ben
reader.ja: 手全体に、まだ焼けるような痛みがあります。
reader.en: I still feel burning pain across my hand.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 店長のロレナは水ぶくれの周りの広い赤みを見ます。
reader.en: Manager Lorena sees a broad area of redness around the blister.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: ロレナは圧迫せずに、清潔なガーゼで火傷を覆います。
reader.en: Lorena covers the burn with clean gauze without pressing.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: ベン、水ぶくれをつぶさないで。今から診療所へ行こう。
reader.en: Ben, do not pop the blister. Let’s go to the clinic now.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: この火傷を事故記録に書いていただけますか。
reader.en: Could you record this burn in the incident log?

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: 午後二時十五分と、目撃したジュリアンの名前を記録します。
reader.en: I will record 2:15 p.m. and the name of Julián, who witnessed it.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: 報告書の写しをいただけますか。
reader.en: Could I have a copy of the report?

reader.speaker: Manager
reader.ja: はい。署名した写しはこちらです。
reader.en: Yes. Here is a signed copy.

reader.speaker: Claire
reader.ja: 一番近い診療所はどこですか。どう行けばいいですか。
reader.en: Where is the nearest clinic, and how do we get there?

reader.speaker: Manager

reader.en: There is a clinic two streets away. Go right along the main street.

lessons.title: 表示されていなかったピーナッツソースを確認する
lessons.objective: Explain a peanut-allergen near miss without blame, name the epinephrine auto-injector and possible serious reaction directly, and agree on concrete checks for the next order.
lessons.focus: もし聞かなかったら…かもしれませんでした describes a near miss. ～と伝えました reports the allergy disclosure, and 次回は…ます assigns future checks without blame.
lessons.scene: Grace notices an unlisted peanut sauce beside a lunch dish before tasting it and speaks with the manager.

エピネフリン自己注射器
注文するときにピーナッツアレルギーを伝えました。
cards.en: I told the server about my peanut allergy when I ordered.

cards.ja: 食べる前に聞いたら、ソースにピーナッツが入っていると分かりました。
cards.en: I asked before eating and learned that the sauce contains peanuts.

cards.ja: 彼女は何も食べていません。
cards.en: She has not eaten any of it.

cards.ja: 彼女はエピネフリン自己注射器をかばんに入れています。
cards.en: She has an epinephrine auto-injector in her bag.

cards.ja: もし聞かなかったら、重いアレルギー反応が起きたかもしれません。
cards.en: If she had not asked, she might have had a serious allergic reaction.

cards.ja: 誰かを責めたいのではありません。次に同じことが起きないようにしたいんです。
cards.en: We are not here to blame anyone. We want to prevent the same thing next time.

cards.ja: アレルギーは注文票に書かれていましたか。
cards.en: Was the allergy written on the order ticket?

cards.ja: 出す前に、料理ごとに厨房へ確認していただけますか。
cards.en: Could you confirm each dish with the kitchen before serving it?

cards.ja: 次回は注文するときにアレルギーカードを見せます。
cards.en: Next time, we will show the allergy card when ordering.

cards.ja: 確認してくださってありがとうございます。

cards.en: We will not serve it without the cook’s confirmation.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 正午、グレースと友人のトマスは小さな食堂で昼食を食べています。
reader.en: At noon, Grace and her friend Tomás are eating lunch at a small restaurant.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: グレースにはピーナッツアレルギーがあり、注文時に店員のアンドレスへ伝えました。
reader.en: Grace has a peanut allergy and told server Andrés when ordering.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 料理の横に茶色いソースがあり、メニューには材料が書かれていません。

reader.en: I want to ask before eating. What is in this sauce?

reader.en: It is peanut sauce.

reader.en: May we speak with manager Verónica?

reader.speaker: Tomás
reader.ja: 誰かを責めたいのではありません。次に同じことが起きないようにしたいんです。
reader.en: We are not here to blame anyone. We want to prevent the same thing next time.

reader.speaker: Tomás

reader.en: Starting today, the server and cook will double-check.

reader.speaker: Tomás
reader.ja: 出す前に、料理ごとに厨房へ確認していただけますか。
reader.en: Could you confirm each dish with the kitchen before serving it?

reader.speaker: Verónica
reader.ja: はい。調理人の確認なしには出しません。
reader.en: Yes. We will not serve it without the cook’s confirmation.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 調理人は清潔な調理器具で、じゃがいものお焼きとアボカド、卵を用意します。
reader.en: The cook uses clean utensils to prepare potato patties, avocado, and egg.

reader.speaker: Cook

reader.en: This dish has no peanuts.

reader.speaker: Tomás
reader.ja: 次回は注文するときにアレルギーカードを見せます。
reader.en: Next time, we will show the allergy card when ordering.

reader.speaker: Tomás
reader.ja: 確認してくださってありがとうございます。
reader.en: Thank you for checking.

lessons.objective: Give a health inspector a formal, precise account of the chicken salad, service time, subsequent nausea, vomiting and fever, and the evidence and consent boundaries.

lessons.title: 一週間のお礼と送別昼食の条件を伝える

lessons.title: 長い昼食を案内し問題を解決する総仕上げ
lessons.objective: Lead a group lunch from menu explanations and a sold-out dish through a shellfish-allergen near miss, written incident report, itemized bill, tip/service-charge question, separate payment and fair review.
lessons.focus: ～なら offers a substitute; ～が入っていますか asks an exact allergen question; 厨房に確認していただけますか requires verification; 明細／別々に払う handle the bill.
lessons.scene: A group visits a hillside seafood restaurant with a Japanese-speaking local guide; one guest has a shellfish allergy.

reader.en: I explain the menu to my friends.

reader.en: Sam has a severe shellfish allergy, so he orders a dish without shellfish.

reader.en: Wait. Sam has a severe shellfish allergy. Please do not eat that dish yet.

reader.en: Does this sauce contain shrimp or other shellfish?

reader.speaker: Me

reader.en: Could you confirm with the kitchen before Sam eats it?

reader.speaker: Me

reader.en: Please remake the dish without shrimp using clean utensils.

reader.en: Manager, I am not assigning blame, but could you record this incident?

reader.speaker: Narrator

reader.speaker: Me
reader.ja: 支払う前に、明細を一緒に確認しましょう。
reader.en: Let’s check the itemized breakdown together before paying.

reader.speaker: Me

reader.en: Patricio, is the service charge included? Is the tip optional?

reader.speaker: Patricio

reader.speaker: Me
reader.ja: 別々に払えますか。

reader.en: Yes, you can pay separately.

reader.speaker: Me
reader.ja: 問題はありましたが、店員はすぐに対応してくれました。
reader.en: There was a problem, but the staff responded quickly.
